clue.text: Pun about helper working as a volunteer?

indicators.note: about suggests the letters of the word before it are turned around and jumbled

parts.note: a helper is an aid, someone or something that assists

explanation.surface: A joke about an assistant who works for nothing, as if the wordplay were a gag in itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Volunteers give their labour for free, so someone volunteering is by nature not paid.

clue.text: Consumed by fashionable South African furniture, one's voracious

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
SA is the abbreviation for South Africa or South African

indicators.note: something consumed by another is swallowed up inside it, so the next piece sits within the earlier ones

parts.note: a table is a piece of furniture
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A hungry person devouring the trendy furniture from South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after one stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A voracious appetite can never be satisfied, which is what insatiable describes.

clue.text: Bent figure study, extremely clunky

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number
a den is a private room for study or work

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extremes of the next word, its first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A bent figure in a study looking awkward and clunky.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural inclination, the same as a tendency.

clue.text: Drink after drink — going topless, very laid back

indicators.note: after places the first drink's letters following the second drink's in the answer

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: going topless removes the top, the first letter, of the word it applies to

parts.note: wine is a drink

explanation.surface: Drink after drink, then off with the shirt: a very relaxed holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' drops the first letter of the earlier drink only.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying flat on one's back, so very literally laid back.

clue.text: It's vital swimming in rough sea to look forward with relish to good food

definitions.text: to look forward with relish to good food

indicators.note: in places the swimming letters inside the rough ones
rough sea is churned up, so its letters are mixed
swimming suggests the letters are moving about and rearranged

explanation.surface: It's vital to swim in rough sea to build an appetite for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams, signalled by 'rough' and 'swimming', the second nested inside the first; 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Salivating, producing saliva, is what the mouth does in eager anticipation of a meal.

clue.text: Oil production in South American country's very risky

indicators.note: in places the produced letters within the country's name

parts.note: Peru is a South American country; with 's it gives PERUS

indicators.note: production here means the letters are worked up into a new form

explanation.surface: Oil production in Peru is a very risky business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' is the anagram signal; the country's possessive 's supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Perilous means full of peril or danger, that is, very risky.

clue.text: False name employed in evident chicanery

indicators.note: employed in puts the letter for name to work inside the other letters
chicanery is trickery, so the letters are deceptively rearranged

explanation.surface: A false name used in obvious trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicanery' rearranges EVIDENT, and N goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An invented story is made up rather than true, hence false.

clue.text: Nick, having very old wife, finally says: 'Enter a nunnery!'

parts.note: to nick is to steal, to take

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Nick, wed to a very old wife, finally tells someone: get thee to a nunnery, as Hamlet tells Ophelia.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman entering a nunnery makes solemn religious promises of poverty, chastity and obedience.

clue.text: Free up king's ceremonial weapon

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to rid is to free, as in rid of pests
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: Free up the king's ceremonial weapon from its display.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirk is a Scottish dagger, worn with Highland dress on ceremonial occasions.

clue.text: Latin song by tenor: The Cowboy's Accessory

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: Reads like a programme listing: a Latin song by a tenor titled The Cowboy's Accessory.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso, the rope a cowboy carries for catching cattle.

clue.text: Aircraft manufacturer, Dr Kee's manoeuvring guide

parts.note: BAE Systems is the British aerospace manufacturer

indicators.note: manoeuvring moves things around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plane maker and Dr Kee's manoeuvres, as if the doctor were a test pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' rearranges DR KEE into DEKER; the 's after Kee is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Baedeker was a famous series of German travel handbooks, so the name came to mean any guidebook.

clue.text: Farewell drink interrupts Victor's speech

indicators.note: a drink that interrupts something breaks into it, so it sits inside

parts.note: Victor is the NATO alphabet word for V
diction is manner of speech
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: Victor's farewell speech is interrupted while he takes a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A valediction is a formal goodbye, a parting address.

clue.text: Snogged after party, Jersey-style?

indicators.note: after places the snogging word following the party word

parts.note: a crew is a party or group of people
to neck is to kiss passionately, to snog

explanation.surface: Kissing after a party, in the manner of the island of Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: A jersey is a pullover, and a crew neck is one with a round neckline; Jersey the island is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Crew-necked describes a sweater with a close round collar, a common style of jersey.

clue.text: Right time to burst above the ground, like a tube

indicators.note: to burst into something is to break inside it, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: aerial means existing above the ground, in the air

explanation.surface: The right moment for something to burst up above ground, like a tube train.
explanation.walkthrough: RT bursts into AERIAL after its first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Arteries are the body's tubes carrying blood, so arterial suggests a main channel shaped like one.

clue.text: After exploit, the woman's down

indicators.note: After places the woman's word following the exploit

parts.note: a feat is an exploit, a daring deed
hers means belonging to the woman

explanation.surface: After her great exploit, the woman is feeling down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like low spirits, but it is the soft fluffy covering of birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is a bird's fine soft plumage, a kind of feathers.

clue.text: Roll along clumsily? Not ruled out when short of oxygen

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order, rearranged

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Something rolling awkwardly, a possibility not ruled out after running short of air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when short of' drops the O of oxygen from NOT RULED, and 'out' rearranges the remaining NTRULED.
explanation.definitionFit: To trundle is to move heavily and slowly, usually on wheels.

clue.text: Slim, stop crushing Rex!

indicators.note: crushing means squeezing something in the middle, so the king's letter is held inside

parts.note: to decease is to die, to stop living
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A sharp order to someone to lose weight and quit squashing poor Rex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stop' for DECEASE is loose: dying is when life stops. 'Slim' is a verb here, to reduce.
explanation.definitionFit: To slim something down is to reduce it, which is to decrease it.

clue.text: Elder's after nook for ornamental garden feature

indicators.note: after places the elder's word following the nook

parts.note: a bay is a recess or nook, as in a bay window
an elder is a tree; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: An old person goes after a quiet nook in a decorative garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elder' seems to be an older person, but it is the elder tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay trees are often clipped into topiary shapes and set in pots as decoration.

clue.text: Suppression of college at one time associated with mental disorder

parts.note: once means at one time, formerly

indicators.note: in disorder the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A college once tried to hush up a case of mental illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Concealment is the hiding or keeping back of something, its suppression.

clue.text: Advanced, gaining ground initially — hour's duration

indicators.note: gaining means taking in another letter inside

parts.note: lent means advanced, as money is advanced on loan

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of the word it follows

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: An army advancing and gaining ground over an hour's duration.
explanation.definitionFit: Length can mean the extent of time something lasts, as in the length of a film.

clue.text: Keen to back singer

indicators.note: to back is to go in reverse, so the singer's word is read backwards

parts.note: a diva is a celebrated female singer

explanation.surface: An eager fan wants to support a singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or enthusiastic, the same as keen.

clue.text: See 7
Force instrument on ex-vice president — no pressure!

parts.note: a viol is an early stringed instrument

indicators.note: no pressure means the pressure letter is removed

parts.note: Mike Pence was US vice president
P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Someone forcing a musical instrument on a former vice president, but gently.
explanation.definitionFit: Violence is the use of physical force to hurt or damage.

clue.text: Tip: one has to be cut for a salad ingredient

parts.note: an end is a tip

indicators.note: to be cut means shortened, as I have is clipped to its contracted form

parts.note: one has is 'I have' with one as I

explanation.surface: Advice that one must trim something before using it in a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be cut' shortens I HAVE to I'VE by losing HA, the contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a leafy chicory plant whose leaves are eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Sid's snapped flower — calamity!

indicators.note: snapped means broken, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Sid has broken the stem of a prized flower: calamity!
explanation.walkthrough: 'snapped' rearranges SID into DIS; the 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden misfortune, the same as a calamity.

clue.text: Holds up part of theatre

definitions.meaning: the seats on a theatre's ground floor

explanation.surface: Delays in the stalls of a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to delay; the stalls are a seating area in a theatre.
